children.innerHTML: Primer exists because our own day ones were 43 tabs and a shrug. We fixed ours, then everyone wanted the fix.

attributes.alt: The Primer team at work in a bright office

children.innerHTML: Primer started as an internal tool at a forty-person startup with a hiring spree and a wiki nobody trusted.
We wrote the first path for one engineer, Nadia. She shipped on day four and asked why the sales team didn't have one. Then the sales team asked. Then our investors' other companies asked.
Six years later the product is bigger and the opinion is the same: onboarding is a path, not a pile of links. Every step has an owner. Progress is public. And the handbook? Retired with honors.
“I stopped being the human FAQ. I miss it zero.”
“Our retention team keeps stealing the format for everything else.”
“Set it up on a Tuesday. New grad shipped Friday.”
A human answers. Usually the same day.

meta_description: The story of Primer: an internal fix for our own bad day ones that everyone else wanted. Say hello, a human answers.
